43.official_section_title: Penalty and compensation for damage to computer, computer system, etc.
43.official_text: If any person without permission of the owner or any other person who is incharge of a computer, computer system or computer network, — (a) accesses or secures access to such computer, computer system or computer network or computer resource... (b) downloads, copies or extracts any data, computer data base or information... (i) destroys, deletes or alters any information residing in a computer resource or diminishes its value or utility or affects it injuriously by any means... he shall be liable to pay damages by way of compensation to the person so affected.
43.simplified_explanation: Imposes civil liability and financial compensation on anyone who accesses another person's device, account, or network without authorization, steals data, or introduces disruptive software.
43.applicability_notes: Applies to unauthorized account access, SIM swapping disrupting network connectivity, predatory loan apps extracting contacts, and remote screen-sharing tools installed deceitfully.

43a.official_section_title: Compensation for failure to protect data
43a.official_text: Where a body corporate, possessing, dealing or handling any sensitive personal data or information in a computer resource which it owns, controls or operates, is negligent in implementing and maintaining reasonable security practices and procedures and thereby causes wrongful loss or wrongful gain to any person, such body corporate shall be liable to pay damages by way of compensation to the person so affected.
43a.simplified_explanation: Requires companies, banks, and online platforms to pay compensation to affected citizens if they fail to implement reasonable cybersecurity safeguards resulting in the leak or theft of sensitive personal or financial data.
43a.applicability_notes: Directly relevant where a citizen suffers financial fraud or identity theft due to a data breach at a bank, telecom company, or e-commerce platform.

67.official_text: Whoever publishes or transmits or causes to be published or transmitted in the electronic form, any material which is lascivious or appeals to the prurient interest or if its effect is such as to tend to deprave and corrupt persons who are likely, having regard to all relevant circumstances, to read, see or hear the matter contained or embodied in it, shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and with fine which may extend to five lakh rupees...

72a.official_section_title: Punishment for disclosure of information in breach of lawful contract
72a.official_text: Save as otherwise provided in this Act or any other law for the time being in force, any person including an intermediary who, while providing services under the terms of lawful contract, has secured access to any material containing personal information about another person, with the intent to cause or knowing that he is likely to cause wrongful loss or wrongful gain discloses, without the consent of the person concerned, or in breach of the lawful contract, such material to any other person, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with a fine which may extend to five lakh rupees, or with both.
72a.simplified_explanation: Penalizes employees, service providers, or telecom staff who access personal information under a contract and leak or sell it to unauthorized third parties without customer consent.
72a.applicability_notes: Directly applies to insider corporate data leaks, telecom staff selling call detail records (CDRs), customer KYC leaks, and BPO agent credential trafficking.

79.official_section_title: Exemption from liability of intermediary in certain cases
79.official_text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force but subject to the provisions of sub-sections (2) and (3), an intermediary shall not be liable for any third party information, data, or communication link made available or hosted by him. (3) The provisions of sub-section (1) shall not apply if — (b) upon receiving actual knowledge, or on being notified by the appropriate Government or its agency that any information, data or communication link... is being used to commit the unlawful act, the intermediary fails to expeditiously remove or disable access to that material.
79.simplified_explanation: Sets conditions under which online platforms lose intermediary safe-harbour immunity if they fail to expeditiously take down unlawful content, impersonating profiles, or fraudulent listings upon notification.
79.applicability_notes: Governs platform liability and takedown obligations for social media platforms, search engines, and e-commerce marketplaces hosting fraudulent accounts.

21.official_section_title: Power of Central Authority to issue directions and penalties against false or misleading advertisements
21.official_text: Where the Central Authority is satisfied after an investigation that any advertisement is false or misleading and is prejudicial to the interest of any consumer or is in contravention of consumer rights, it may, by order, issue directions to the concerned trader or manufacturer or endorser or advertiser or publisher to discontinue such advertisement or to modify the same in such manner as may be specified...

35.official_section_title: Manner in which complaint shall be made
35.official_text: A complaint, in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided, may be filed with a District Commission by— (a) the consumer to whom such goods are sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or such service is provided or agreed to be provided; (b) any recognised consumer association...
35.simplified_explanation: Outlines how any citizen or consumer association can formally lodge a complaint before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (or online via e-Daakhil).

84.official_text: A product manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action, if— (a) the product contains a manufacturing defect; or (b) the product is defective in design; or (c) there is a deviation from manufacturing specifications; or (d) the product does not conform to the express warranty; or (e) the product fails to contain adequate instructions of correct usage to prevent any harm or any warning regarding improper or incorrect usage.
84.simplified_explanation: Holds manufacturers legally liable for compensation if a product causes harm, loss, or injury due to manufacturing defects, design flaws, or breach of express warranty.
84.applicability_notes: Directly applies where an electronic appliance, vehicle, machinery, or consumable product has manufacturing defects or fails to honor warranty obligations.

85.official_section_title: Liability of product service provider or product seller
85.official_text: A product seller who is not a product manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action, if— (a) he has exercised substantial control over the designing, testing, manufacturing, packaging or labelling of a product; or (b) he has altered or modified the product and such alteration or modification was the substantial factor in causing the harm; or (c) he has made an express warranty of a product independent of any express warranty made by a manufacturer and such product failed to conform to such warranty...
85.simplified_explanation: Holds product sellers and e-commerce platforms liable under product liability if they gave independent warranties, modified goods, or failed to pass on manufacturer warnings.
85.applicability_notes: Applies where an e-commerce marketplace or local dealer independently promised a warranty or modified the product before delivery.

86.official_text: A product service provider shall be liable in a product liability action, if— (a) the service provided by him was faulty or imperfect or deficient or inadequate in quality, nature or manner of performance which is required to be provided by or under any law for the time being in force, or pursuant to a contract or otherwise; or (b) there was an act of omission or commission or negligence or conscious withholding of any information which caused harm; or (c) the service provider did not issue adequate instructions or warnings to prevent any harm; or (d) the service did not conform to express warranty or the terms and conditions of the contract.

90.official_section_title: Punishment for manufacturing, storing, selling, distributing, or importing products containing adulterant
90.official_text: Whoever, by himself or by any other person on his behalf, manufactures for sale, or stores, or sells, or distributes, or imports any product containing an adulterant which is not injurious to health, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months and with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees; if causing injury not amounting to grievous hurt, imprisonment up to one year and fine up to three lakh rupees; if causing grievous hurt, imprisonment up to seven years and fine up to five lakh rupees; if causing death, imprisonment not less than seven years which may extend to life imprisonment...

18.official_section_title: Powers and functions of Central Authority
18.official_text: (1) The Central Authority shall— (a) protect, promote and enforce the rights of consumers as a class, and prevent violation of consumers rights under this Act; (b) prevent unfair trade practices and ensure that no person engages in unfair trade practices; (c) ensure that no false or misleading advertisement is made of any goods or services which is prejudicial to the interests of consumers or is in contravention of the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder; (d) ensure that no person takes part in the publication of any advertisement which is false or misleading...

25.official_section_title: Agreement without consideration, void, unless it is in writing and registered, or is a promise to compensate for something done, or is a promise to pay a debt barred by limitation law
25.official_text: An agreement made without consideration is void, unless— (1) it is expressed in writing and registered under the law for the time being in force for the registration of documents, and is made on account of natural love and affection between parties standing in a near relation to each other; or (2) it is a promise to compensate, wholly or in part, a person who has already voluntarily done something for the promisor; or (3) it is a promise, made in writing and signed by the person to be charged therewith, or by his agent generally or specially authorized in that behalf, to pay wholly or in part a debt of which the creditor might have enforced payment but for the law for the limitation of suits.
25.simplified_explanation: While agreements without consideration are generally void, a written and signed promise to pay a time-barred debt (under Section 25(3)) is fully valid and legally enforceable in a court of law.

40.official_section_title: Person by whom promise is to be performed
40.official_text: If it appears from the nature of the case that it was the intention of the parties to any contract that any promise contained in it should be performed by the promisor himself, such promise must be performed by the promisor. In other cases, the promisor or his representatives may employ a competent person to perform it.

55.official_section_title: Effect of failure to perform at fixed time, in contract in which time is essential
55.official_text: When a party to a contract promises to do a certain thing at or before a specified time, or certain things at or before specified times, and fails to do any such thing at or before the specified time, the contract, or so much of it as has not been performed, becomes voidable at the option of the promisee, if the intention of the parties was that time should be of the essence of the contract.
55.simplified_explanation: Provides that when time is of the essence of an agreement, failure by a party to perform by the agreed deadline makes the contract voidable at the option of the other party, who can cancel and claim damages.

151.official_section_title: Care to be taken by bailee
151.official_text: In all cases of bailment, the bailee is bound to take as much care of the goods bailed to him as a man of ordinary prudence would, under similar circumstances, take of his own goods of the same bulk, quantity and value as the goods bailed.

62.official_section_title: Effect of novation, rescission, and alteration of contract

(2) Offence shall be inquired into and tried only by a court within whose local jurisdiction the branch of the bank where the payee maintains the account is situated.
142.simplified_explanation: Mandates strict statutory timelines: Legal demand notice must be dispatched within 30 days of bank memo. Drawer has 15 days to pay. Complaint must be filed before the Judicial Magistrate within 30 days after the 15-day period expires. Jurisdiction is where the payee holds their bank account.
142.applicability_notes: Strict limitation requirement: failure to serve notice within 30 days or file complaint within 1 month defeats the criminal remedy.

105.official_text: A lease of immoveable property is a transfer of a right to enjoy such property, made for a certain time, express or implied, or in perpetuity, in consideration of a price paid or promised, or of money, a share of crops, service or any other thing of value, to be rendered periodically or on specified occasions to the transferor by the transferee, who accepts the transfer on such terms.
105.simplified_explanation: Defines a tenancy/lease as the legal transfer of the right to occupy and enjoy property for a specified period in exchange for agreed rental consideration.
105.applicability_notes: Statutory foundation for all residential and commercial tenancy agreements and landlord-tenant relationships.

106.official_section_title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract (Notice to Quit)
106.official_text: (1) In the absence of a contract or local law or usage to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for agricultural or manufacturing purposes shall be deemed to be a lease from year to year, terminable, on the part of either lessor or lessee, by six months' notice; and a lease of immovable property for any other purpose shall be deemed to be a lease from month to month, terminable, on the part of either lessor or lessee, by fifteen days' notice.
106.simplified_explanation: In the absence of an express contrary clause, residential and commercial leases require a mandatory 15-day written notice to quit expiring with the end of a tenancy month. Landlords cannot unilaterally evict tenants without statutory notice.
106.applicability_notes: Protects tenants from immediate arbitrary eviction and governs legal termination of lease agreements.

108.official_section_title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee (Security Deposit refund)
108.official_text: In the absence of a contract or local usage to the contrary, the lessor and the lessee of immovable property, as against one another, respectively, possess the rights and are subject to the liabilities... The lessor is bound to disclose to the lessee any material defect in the property... and is bound to ensure peaceful enjoyment... and on termination the lessee is bound to put the lessor into possession, whereupon the lessor is bound to return the advance/security deposit after lawful deductions.
108.simplified_explanation: Governs statutory rights and obligations: Lessor must disclose latent property defects and guarantee quiet possession. Lessee must pay rent and maintain premises. Upon peaceful handover, the landlord is legally obligated to refund the security deposit, deducting only verified unpaid dues or agreed repairs.
108.applicability_notes: Primary statutory remedy for arbitrary security deposit withholding, unjustified painting deductions, or denial of tenant refund.

111.official_text: A lease of immoveable property determines— (a) by efflux of the time limited thereby; (b) where such time is limited conditionally on the happening of some event, by the happening of such event; (c) by the interest of the lessor in the property terminating... (g) by forfeiture; (h) on the expiration of a notice to determine the lease, or to quit.
111.simplified_explanation: Lists the exact legal grounds on which a tenancy terminates, including expiry of agreed duration, surrender, or expiry of a valid statutory notice to quit.
111.applicability_notes: Prevents landlords from declaring unlawful premature termination or illegal lockouts.

art_55.official_section_title: Schedule Article 55 - Limitation for breach of contract
art_55.official_text: Description of suit: For compensation for the breach of any contract, express or implied not herein specially provided for. Period of limitation: Three years. Time from which period begins to run: When the contract is broken or (where there are successive breaches) when the breach in respect of which the suit is instituted occurs or (where the breach is continuing) when it ceases.
art_55.simplified_explanation: A civil suit for damages or compensation for breach of contract must be filed within 3 years from the date the contract was broken.
art_55.applicability_notes: Statutory timeline for filing commercial contract damages, vendor defaults, and freelancer payment suits in civil court.

art_7.official_section_title: Schedule Article 7 - Limitation for recovery of wages
art_7.official_text: Description of suit: For wages in the case of any other person. Period of limitation: Three years. Time from which period begins to run: When the wages accrue due.
art_7.simplified_explanation: A civil suit or statutory recovery claim for unpaid wages, salary arrears, or professional remuneration must be filed within 3 years from the date the wages accrued due.
art_7.applicability_notes: Governs the time limit for employees and contractors to recover pending compensation in court.

5.official_text: (1) The wages of every person employed upon or in— (a) any railway, factory or industrial or other establishment upon or in which less than one thousand persons are employed, shall be paid before the expiry of the seventh day, (b) any other establishment, shall be paid before the expiry of the tenth day, after the last day of the wage-period... 7.official_section_title: Deductions which may be made from wages
7.official_text: (1) Notwithstanding the provisions of any contract, the wages of an employed person shall be paid to him without deductions of any kind except those authorised by or under this Act... (2) Deductions from the wages of an employed person shall be made only in accordance with the provisions of this Act (fines, absence from duty, damage to property entrusted, income-tax, PF contributions, loan recovery).
7.simplified_explanation: An employer is strictly prohibited from making arbitrary salary cuts. Only deductions specifically authorized by statute (PF, tax, absence from duty, or proven entrusted damage) are lawful. All other unilateral deductions are illegal wage theft.
7.applicability_notes: Primary weapon against arbitrary penalty deductions, training bond deductions, and exit laptop withholdings.

15.official_section_title: Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment
15.official_text: (1) The appropriate Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint a presiding officer of any Labour Court or other officer with experience as a Judge... to be the authority to hear and decide for any specified area all claims arising out of deductions from wages, or delay in payment of the wages... 15.simplified_explanation: Employees can file an application before the Payment of Wages Authority for delayed salary or unlawful deductions. The Authority has the power to order payment of the withheld wages along with compensation up to 10 times the deducted amount.

12.official_section_title: Payment of minimum rates of wages
12.official_text: (1) Where in respect of any scheduled employment a notification under section 5 is in force, the employer shall pay to every employee engaged in a scheduled employment under him wages at a rate not less than the minimum rate of wages fixed by such notification for that class of employees in that employment without any deductions except as may be authorised within such time and subject to such conditions as may be prescribed.
12.simplified_explanation: Every employer must pay workers wages not less than the statutory minimum wage rates fixed by state or central notifications. Paying below minimum wage is a non-negotiable statutory violation.
12.applicability_notes: Applies to daily wage earners, contract workers, security staff, and entry-level employees across scheduled employments.
